how: Mount Takao in Hachioji has eight marked trails and is about an hour from central Tokyo by train.
Mount Takao's eight mountain trails, reached in about an hour from central Tokyo, are used for hiking and trail running.
Nakano Broadway's upper floors are packed with shops selling figurines, anime merchandise and collectibles, including Mandarake annexes dedicated to toy robots and action figures.
Mandarake's Nakano Broadway store and its specialist annexes sell used manga, comics and doujinshi.
Tufting studio KEKE ran first-time workshops where visitors tuft a small rug from their own design (online booking); the listing is from 2021.
Atelier Little Pottery Studio in Kichijoji teaches wheel throwing to enthusiasts and novices; several other Minato-ku schools offer one-day trial courses.
Atelier Little Pottery Studio in Kichijoji teaches hand-building alongside wheel throwing under experienced instructors.
Tokyo Comedy Bar runs two English-language open mic nights a week plus showcases, so beginners can try a set.
Tokyo Comedy Bar hosts regular improv shows and occasional improv classes and workshops.
Studio JBA runs salsa or bachata lessons on most nights, usually a 7pm beginner class followed by social dancing.
Studio Hougaku Academy teaches taiko from beginner to advanced with bookable one-time trial lessons; sticks are included.
Ance Space Yoyogi is a rental studio used for lessons from tap to house dance and capoeira.
Tokyo Swing Dance Society ran Swing Sundays and Swing Night lessons in English and Japanese (2014 listing).
Architanz offers drop-in ballet classes, with most teachers speaking English (2014 listing).
Fitness Club Hiroo lists flamenco among its dance classes (2014 listing).
Ito Bindery, a family-run bindery in Sumida, hosts a beginner notebook-making experience in Japanese and English.

how: Art Party Tokyo has run beginner calligraphy and sumi-e workshops held in English with no experience needed (2025 sessions listed).
Only Japanese calligraphy (shodo) was found, taught in an English-language beginner workshop at Art Party Tokyo rather than a Chinese-calligraphy school.
Hiro Workshop in Kichijoji teaches small leather goods at all skill levels, with drop-in during opening hours.
Hiro Workshop in Kichijoji also teaches brass and silver jewellery making at all skill levels.
Paper Pool in Yutenji rents a monochrome darkroom by the half hour with chemicals supplied; Tokyo has other rental darkrooms.
Saori Tokyo runs two-hour Saori weaving classes Tuesday to Saturday, with staff demonstrating each step and only a little English spoken.
Ochanomizu Origami Kaikan runs monthly origami workshops that can be taken in English or Japanese.
Tokyo Animation College offers 2- and 3-year full-time animation courses; no short hobby course was confirmed.
Japanorama gives English-language photography lessons and photowalks for beginners (rates from a 2016 page).
FabCafe Tokyo hosts a free monthly drop-in drawing meetup (drink required, booking needed); the listing seen is from 2023.
Hirata Bladesmiths in Ome offers a roughly two-hour knife-forging experience for visitors rather than ongoing smithing classes.
Benkei Fishing Club, a pond in central Tokyo, charges by the half hour and rents rods; bait fishing is beginner-friendly.
Roppongi Tenmon Club holds monthly and moon-viewing sessions on the Tokyo City View deck, limited by city light pollution.
Tokyo has many active geocaches, including one by the Hachiko statue in Shibuya and the most-favourited cache in Japan at Kaminarimon, Asakusa.
English-speaking guides lead hiking tours of Mount Takao from Shinjuku Station.
Tokyo Port Wild Bird Park, a Wild Bird Society of Japan sanctuary on reclaimed bay land, is open daily except Mondays for a small entry fee.
The free 599 Museum at the foot of Mount Takao has a large insect section with butterflies displayed by species.
Harajuku and Shibuya have dozens of sneaker shops such as Kicks Lab, Worm and Kith Tokyo (browsing is free; purchases cost extra).
Nakano Broadway hosts several vintage and second-hand watch shops such as Jack Road, alongside shops in Ginza, Morishita and Shinjuku.
Akihabara has many card shops; Card Lab (C-Labo) in the Radio Kaikan building has a 64-seat dueling venue.
Whale watching in Tokyo Metropolis means the Ogasawara Islands, about 1,000 km away on a roughly 24-hour ferry; there is no regular whale-watching in Tokyo Bay.
Shimamura Music Store's Ikebukuro Piano Salon gives private adult piano lessons in English, with a 30-minute trial.
